components.note: 厂 (cliff, shelter) — 厂 is a cliff or overhang and the root of 厅, 原, 厚; the modern meaning "factory" is separate, as in 工厂.

example.hanzi: 他在一家工厂工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
example.english: He works in a factory.
example.fact: 厂 is the simplified writing of 廠 'factory' and forms 工厂, 厂长 (factory director) and 钢厂. The same shape is also the 'cliff' radical (read hǎn), which sits at the upper left of many characters.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸在钢厂工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zài gāngchǎng gōngzuò.
examples.english: My dad works at a steel mill.

examples.hanzi: 这座厂房已经很旧了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chǎngfáng yǐjīng hěn jiù le.
examples.english: This factory building is already very old.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赖 is to depend on, or to default on a debt.
剌 (là) hints at the sound: 赖 lài is close, as in 癞 lài and 籁 lài.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的味道真不赖。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de wèidào zhēn bù lài.
example.english: This restaurant's food really isn't bad.
example.fact: Michelin, the tire company, began publishing its restaurant guide in 1900 to encourage French motorists to drive more and wear out their tires faster, only later evolving the guide's star ratings into the internationally respected culinary benchmark they are today. Its anonymous inspectors' identities remain a closely guarded secret even now.

examples.hanzi: 你的中文说得真不赖！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn búlài!
examples.english: Your Chinese is not bad at all!

examples.hanzi: 这部电影还不赖，值得一看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hái búlài, zhídé yí kàn.
examples.english: This movie isn't bad and is worth watching.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 这座城市的人口已经超过一千万。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de rénkǒu yǐjīng chāoguò yī qiān wàn.
example.english: This city's population has already exceeded ten million.
example.fact: The world's human population passed 8 billion in November 2022, yet demographers project growth will slow sharply and possibly peak later this century, according to United Nations projections, as birth rates fall in more and more countries. Some nations, including Japan and South Korea, are already seeing population decline rather than growth.

examples.hanzi: 中国的人口非常多。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de rénkǒu fēicháng duō.
examples.english: China has a very large population.

examples.hanzi: 这个村子只有几百人口。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi zhǐ yǒu jǐ bǎi rénkǒu.
examples.english: This village has only a few hundred inhabitants.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 这位年轻画家因为一幅画而出名。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi niánqīng huàjiā yīnwèi yī fú huà ér chūmíng.
example.english: This young painter became famous because of one painting.
example.fact: Vincent van Gogh sold only a single painting during his lifetime and died largely unrecognized in 1890, yet within a few decades his work became some of the most valuable and famous in art history. His sister-in-law Johanna is largely credited with promoting his paintings and letters after his death, building the reputation he never lived to see.

examples.hanzi: 这个地方因为美食而出名。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfang yīnwèi měishí ér chūmíng.
examples.english: This place is famous for its food.

examples.hanzi: 他想靠唱歌出名。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng kào chànggē chūmíng.
examples.english: He wants to become famous through singing.

components.note: 大 (person) — a person squeezed between two smaller figures 人 on either side: to clamp or wedge in.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 他穿着一件黑色的夹克出门了。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yī jiàn hēisè de jiākè chūmén le.
example.english: He went out wearing a black jacket.
example.fact: The zipper, patented in 1913 by Gideon Sundback, wasn't widely used in jackets until the 1920s when tailors adopted it for work clothes and, later, for the leather flight jackets worn by World War I aviators — before that, clothing relied mainly on buttons and hooks.

examples.hanzi: 今天有点冷，你最好带上夹克。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒudiǎn lěng, nǐ zuì hǎo dài shàng jiākè.
examples.english: It's a bit cold today, so you'd better bring a jacket.

examples.hanzi: 这件夹克的颜色很适合你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn jiākè de yánsè hěn shìhé nǐ.
examples.english: The color of this jacket really suits you.

components.note: 车 (vehicle, simplified 車) — the left part, as in 轮 wheel, 辆; the right part 欠 is no real sound clue for ruǎn.

example.hanzi: 这张沙发很软。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng shāfā hěn ruǎn.
example.english: This sofa is very soft.
example.fact: 软 is the opposite of 硬, hence 软件 (software) vs 硬件 (hardware). It also describes weakness or leniency: 软弱 (weak), 心软 (soft-hearted), and 软卧 (soft sleeper) is a train class in China.

examples.hanzi: 这个枕头又轻又软。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhěntou yòu qīng yòu ruǎn.
examples.english: This pillow is light and soft.

examples.hanzi: 他是做软件开发的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zuò ruǎnjiàn kāifā de.
examples.english: He works in software development.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 违 is to go against or part from.
韦 (wéi) gives the sound exactly: 违 wéi, also in 围 wéi and 伟 wěi.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 在这个国家赌博是违法的。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège guójiā dǔbó shì wéifǎ de.
example.english: Gambling is illegal in this country.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a nearly eight-foot basalt stele around 1754 BC, is one of the earliest written legal codes still largely intact — its 282 laws covered everything from theft to divorce and famously prescribed 'an eye for an eye' punishments.

examples.hanzi: 开车的时候打电话是违法的。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou dǎ diànhuà shì wéifǎ de.
examples.english: Talking on the phone while driving is illegal.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司因为违法经营被罚款了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yīnwèi wéifǎ jīngyíng bèi fákuǎn le.
examples.english: This company was fined for operating illegally.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.
氵 (water radical) — 派 first meant a stream branching off a river, which grew into branch, faction and to send out.

example.hanzi: 那个城市里有好几个帮派互相争夺地盘。
example.pinyin: Nàge chéngshì lǐ yǒu hǎo jǐ gè bāngpài hùxiāng zhēngduó dìpán.
example.english: There are several gangs in that city fighting over turf.
example.fact: Sicily's Cosa Nostra traces its roots to 19th-century rural militias hired to protect landowners' estates; historians often point to the island's fragmented, feudal countryside as fertile ground for the loosely federated, family-based criminal organizations that emerged from it.

examples.hanzi: 他年轻时加入过一个帮派，后来后悔了。
examples.pinyin: Tā niánqīng shí jiārù guo yí gè bāngpài, hòulái hòuhuǐ le.
examples.english: He joined a gang when he was young and later regretted it.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲了两个帮派之间的斗争。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng le liǎng gè bāngpài zhījiān de dòuzhēng.
examples.english: This film is about the struggle between two gangs.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院, 队; hiding behind a mound — 隐 is to conceal; the right side is a simplified stand-in.
禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.

example.hanzi: 很多人担心社交媒体会侵犯他们的隐私。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén dānxīn shèjiāo méitǐ huì qīnfàn tāmen de yǐnsī.
example.english: Many people worry that social media will invade their privacy.
example.fact: The right to privacy as a distinct legal concept was first articulated in an 1890 Harvard Law Review article by Samuel Warren and Louis Brandeis, written partly in response to intrusive newspaper coverage of Warren's own family — it later shaped landmark U.S. Supreme Court privacy rulings.

examples.hanzi: 请尊重别人的隐私，不要乱翻他的手机。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zūnzhòng biéren de yǐnsī, bú yào luàn fān tā de shǒujī.
examples.english: Please respect others' privacy and don't go through his phone.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的隐私，我不想告诉你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de yǐnsī, wǒ bù xiǎng gàosu nǐ.
examples.english: That's private, and I don't want to tell you.

components.note: 行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 周末街头挤满了逛街的人。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò jiētóu jǐmǎn le guàngjiē de rén.
example.english: On the weekend the streets were packed with shoppers.
example.fact: Pompeii's streets, preserved under volcanic ash since 79 AD, still show worn ruts from cart wheels and raised stepping stones that let pedestrians cross without stepping in flooded gutters — an ancient solution to the same street-drainage problem modern cities still wrestle with.

examples.hanzi: 街头有一位老人在拉二胡。
examples.pinyin: Jiētóu yǒu yí wèi lǎorén zài lā èrhú.
examples.english: An old man is playing the erhu on the street.

examples.hanzi: 这家小吃店就在街头拐角处。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎochī diàn jiù zài jiētóu guǎijiǎo chù.
examples.english: This snack shop is right at the street corner.

components.note: 角 (horn) — 角 as in 解 untie: 触 first meant to butt with horns, then to touch.
虫 (chóng) — not a reliable sound clue — 触 is chù; the traditional 觸 had 蜀 (shǔ) giving the sound, and 虫 is its remnant.

example.hanzi: 别触碰那个红色的按钮。
example.pinyin: Bié chùpèng nàge hóngsè de ànniǔ.
example.english: Don't touch that red button.
example.fact: 触 originally pictured butting with horns and now means 'to touch': 接触 (contact), 触摸屏 (touchscreen), 触动 (to stir the heart). 触 is not a spoken word on its own; it usually appears in compounds.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事深深地触动了我。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi shēnshēn de chùdòng le wǒ.
examples.english: This story deeply moved me.

examples.hanzi: 屏幕可以用手指触摸。
examples.pinyin: Píngmù kěyǐ yòng shǒuzhǐ chùmō.
examples.english: The screen can be touched with a finger.

components.note: 鼠 (rat) — a picture of a rat with its teeth (臼 on top) and a tail; as a radical it is in rodent names.

example.hanzi: 猫在抓老鼠。
example.pinyin: Māo zài zhuā lǎoshǔ.
example.english: The cat is catching a mouse.
example.fact: Chinese does not distinguish mouse from rat: 老鼠 covers both. 鼠 is the first animal in the zodiac, and 鼠标 ('mouse mark') is the computer mouse.

examples.hanzi: 他用鼠标点了一下按钮。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shǔbiāo diǎn le yíxià ànniǔ.
examples.english: He clicked the button with the mouse.

examples.hanzi: 仓鼠在笼子里跑步。
examples.pinyin: Cāngshǔ zài lóngzi li pǎobù.
examples.english: The hamster is running in its cage.

components.note: 阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — hills and heights, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sunny side, 队 team.

example.hanzi: 陈老师教我们数学。
example.pinyin: Chén lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen shùxué.
example.english: Teacher Chen teaches us math.
example.fact: 陈 is one of the most common surnames. As a word it means 'to arrange or display' (陈列) and 'old, stale' (陈旧, 陈醋 'aged vinegar').

examples.hanzi: 陈先生是我们的新邻居。
examples.pinyin: Chén xiānsheng shì wǒmen de xīn línjū.
examples.english: Mr. Chen is our new neighbor.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶酒是陈年的好酒。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng jiǔ shì chénnián de hǎo jiǔ.
examples.english: This bottle is a fine aged wine.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 她在行李箱里放了几件内衣。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xínglixiāng lǐ fàng le jǐ jiàn nèiyī.
example.english: She packed a few pieces of underwear in her suitcase.
example.fact: Archaeologists found a roughly 600-year-old linen bra among artifacts in an Austrian castle in 2008, pushing back the known history of supportive women's undergarments by centuries — before the find, bras were generally thought to be a 19th-century invention.

examples.hanzi: 这个牌子的内衣穿起来很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhège páizi de nèiyī chuān qǐlái hěn shūfu.
examples.english: Underwear from this brand is comfortable to wear.

examples.hanzi: 我要去商场买几件新内衣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù shāngchǎng mǎi jǐ jiàn xīn nèiyī.
examples.english: I'm going to the mall to buy a few new pieces of underwear.

components.note: 自 (self/nose) — the middle part, as in 臭 smell; it does not explain 'summer'. Memory aid: your own nose feeling the heat.
夂 (go slowly) — the bottom part and radical, a foot. The old form shows a figure in ceremonial dress; as a memory aid only.
女 (woman) — traditional reading shows an axe-like weapon 戌 over a woman 女, hence power and authority; compare 姑 and 妈.
夷 (yí) — an old word for eastern tribes; as a part it sounds out 姨 yí, 痍 yí and 胰 yí.

example.hanzi: 我们计划明年夏天去夏威夷旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà míngnián xiàtiān qù Xiàwēiyí lǚxíng.
example.english: We're planning to travel to Hawaii next summer.
example.fact: The Hawaiian Islands formed one by one as the Pacific tectonic plate slid slowly over a stationary hotspot of rising magma; because the plate keeps moving northwest, the islands get progressively older in that direction, with the still-erupting Big Island the youngest of the chain.

examples.hanzi: 夏威夷的海滩非常漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Xiàwēiyí de hǎitān fēicháng piàoliang.
examples.english: The beaches in Hawaii are beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 你去过夏威夷吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù guo Xiàwēiyí ma?
examples.english: Have you ever been to Hawaii?

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: achievement takes effort.
工 (gōng) gives the exact sound; 工 also means work.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 这款手机有很多实用的功能。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī yǒu hěn duō shíyòng de gōngnéng.
example.english: This phone has many practical functions.
example.fact: The human appendix, long dismissed as a useless evolutionary leftover, is now believed by many biologists to serve as a safe house for beneficial gut bacteria, letting the digestive system quickly recolonize itself with healthy microbes after a severe bout of illness like diarrhea.

examples.hanzi: 这台洗衣机有烘干功能。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái xǐyījī yǒu hōnggān gōngnéng.
examples.english: This washing machine has a drying function.

examples.hanzi: 肝脏的主要功能是帮助消化。
examples.pinyin: Gānzàng de zhǔyào gōngnéng shì bāngzhù xiāohuà.
examples.english: The main function of the liver is to aid digestion.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals and money: 钱, 铁, 钢; 银 is silver.
艮 (gèn) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 根 gēn and 眼 yǎn.

example.hanzi: 她戴着一条银项链。
example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì tiáo yín xiàngliàn.
example.english: She is wearing a silver necklace.
example.fact: 银 is silver and, because silver was once the currency, it stands in money words: 银行 (bank, literally 'silver firm'), 银牌 (silver medal) and 银色 (silver color). 水银 is mercury, 'water-silver'.

examples.hanzi: 我要去银行取钱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yínháng qǔ qián.
examples.english: I'm going to the bank to withdraw money.

examples.hanzi: 这个银勺子是奶奶送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yín sháozi shì nǎinai sòng de.
examples.english: This silver spoon was a gift from Grandma.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稳 is firm, steady, like a solid harvest.

example.hanzi: 这座桥很稳。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo hěn wěn.
example.english: This bridge is very stable.
example.fact: 稳 is a common description of calm and reliability: 稳定 (stable), 稳重 (sedate), 稳妥 (safe). In slang, 稳了 means 'it's in the bag': 这次考试稳了 ('I'm sure to pass this test').

examples.hanzi: 请站稳,公交车要开了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhàn wěn, gōngjiāochē yào kāi le.
examples.english: Please hold steady; the bus is about to leave.

examples.hanzi: 他的工作很稳定。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngzuò hěn wěndìng.
examples.english: His job is very stable.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
七 (qī) — seven; as a part it sounds out 切 qiē (cut, with 刀 knife) and 柒 qī.

example.hanzi: 这是他第七次参加马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā dì qī cì cānjiā mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: This is the seventh time he has taken part in a marathon.
example.fact: Saturn is the seventh planet counting outward from the Sun, but it was the last of the seven 'classical planets' visible to the naked eye — the ones ancient astronomers could track across the sky without any telescope.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中得了第七名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le dì-qī míng.
examples.english: He came in seventh in the competition.

examples.hanzi: 我住在这栋楼的第七层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài zhè dòng lóu de dì-qī céng.
examples.english: I live on the seventh floor of this building.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.

example.hanzi: 老师明确地解释了考试的规则。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī míngquè de jiěshì le kǎoshì de guīzé.
example.english: The teacher clearly explained the rules for the exam.
example.fact: The Plain Writing Act, signed into U.S. law in 2010, requires federal agencies to write public documents in clear, direct language — follow-up studies found that plainly written government forms cut citizen error rates and call-center volume by as much as half.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一个明确的答复。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí gè míngquè de dáfù.
examples.english: Please give me a clear answer.

examples.hanzi: 我们要先明确目标，再制定计划。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xiān míngquè mùbiāo, zài zhìdìng jìhuà.
examples.english: We should clarify our goal first and then make a plan.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 他说英语带有很重的法国口音。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō Yīngyǔ dài yǒu hěn zhòng de Fǎguó kǒuyīn.
example.english: He speaks English with a heavy French accent.
example.fact: Foreign accent syndrome is a rare neurological condition, usually triggered by a stroke or brain injury, in which patients suddenly begin speaking their own native language with what sounds like a foreign accent — fewer than 100 cases have been documented worldwide since it was first described in 1907.

examples.hanzi: 听口音，他应该是北方人。
examples.pinyin: Tīng kǒuyīn, tā yīnggāi shì běifāngrén.
examples.english: Judging from his accent, he must be a northerner.

examples.hanzi: 她的中文没有口音，说得很标准。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén méiyǒu kǒuyīn, shuō de hěn biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Her Chinese has no accent and is very standard.

components.note: 门 (gate) — marks gates and doors, as in 问, 间, 闪, 开; 闯 shows a horse 马 bursting through a gate.
马 (horse) — the charging animal, as in 骑 ride, 骂.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 一只野猫闯入了我们的花园。
example.pinyin: Yī zhī yěmāo chuǎngrù le wǒmen de huāyuán.
example.english: A wild cat broke into our garden.
example.fact: In 2020, wild boars increasingly wandered into Barcelona's streets and parks as pandemic lockdowns emptied cities of people — a pattern seen in other quiet urban areas too, showing how quickly wildlife adapts to sudden drops in human activity.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚有人闯入了我们的办公室。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn yǒu rén chuǎngrù le wǒmen de bàngōngshì.
examples.english: Someone broke into our office last night.

examples.hanzi: 一个陌生的男人突然闯入了会场。
examples.pinyin: Yí gè mòshēng de nánrén tūrán chuǎngrù le huìchǎng.
examples.english: A strange man suddenly burst into the meeting hall.

components.note: 疋 (foot) — the left side is a flag shape, and a foot following it: turning with the flag, to revolve. 漩 xuán (whirlpool) shares the sound.
车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 摩天轮缓缓地旋转着。
example.pinyin: Mótiānlún huǎnhuǎn de xuánzhuǎn zhe.
example.english: The Ferris wheel slowly rotated.
example.fact: Venus rotates so slowly, and in the opposite direction from most planets, that a single day there — one full rotation — takes about 243 Earth days, longer than the roughly 225 Earth days it takes Venus to complete an orbit around the Sun.

examples.hanzi: 地球一边旋转，一边绕着太阳转。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú yìbiān xuánzhuǎn, yìbiān ràozhe tàiyáng zhuàn.
examples.english: The Earth spins while orbiting the sun.

examples.hanzi: 她在舞台上优美地旋转着。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǔtái shàng yōuměi de xuánzhuǎnzhe.
examples.english: She spun gracefully on the stage.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.
片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards; 牌 is a signboard, a card or a tile.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 牌 pái is close to 脾 pí, which shares it.

example.hanzi: 这个品牌以质量好而出名。
example.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái yǐ zhìliàng hǎo ér chūmíng.
example.english: This brand is known for its high quality.
example.fact: The Bass Red Triangle, used by the British brewer Bass since the 1870s, became the United Kingdom's first registered trademark in 1876 when a new trademark law took effect — legend holds that a company clerk camped outside the registry office overnight to be first in line.

examples.hanzi: 你喜欢哪个品牌的运动鞋？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎge pǐnpái de yùndòngxié?
examples.english: Which brand of sneakers do you like?

examples.hanzi: 他们想打造一个自己的品牌。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiǎng dǎzào yí gè zìjǐ de pǐnpái.
examples.english: They want to build a brand of their own.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 is a hole, as in 空, 窗, 突; 穿 is to pierce through, and the 牙 is a tooth boring in.
走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.

example.hanzi: 这条隧道穿越了整座山。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo suìdào chuānyuè le zhěng zuò shān.
example.english: This tunnel goes through the entire mountain.
example.fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in the Swiss Alps, opened in 2016, runs for about 35 miles beneath the mountains and took 17 years to bore — engineers had to cool the rock face, which reached temperatures above 45°C (113°F) from geothermal heat deep underground.

examples.hanzi: 火车穿越沙漠，驶向远方。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē chuānyuè shāmò, shǐ xiàng yuǎnfāng.
examples.english: The train crosses the desert and heads into the distance.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢看主角穿越到古代的小说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn zhǔjué chuānyuè dào gǔdài de xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: I like novels where the hero time-travels to ancient times.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 他有意避开了这个话题。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒuyì bìkāi le zhège huàtí.
example.english: He intentionally avoided this topic.
example.fact: Studies in cognitive psychology find that people consistently judge accidental harms less severely than intentional ones with identical outcomes — a pattern researchers call the 'intentionality bias,' which shows up even in young children's moral judgments by around age four.

examples.hanzi: 他有意请我们去他家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuyì qǐng wǒmen qù tā jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: He intends to invite us over for dinner.

examples.hanzi: 如果你对这份工作有意，可以投简历。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ duì zhè fèn gōngzuò yǒuyì, kěyǐ tóu jiǎnlì.
examples.english: If you're interested in this job, you can send in your résumé.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头, 题, 顶: to turn the head and look.
厄 stands in for 雇 (gù) in the traditional 顧; the clue is only loose today.

example.hanzi: 年终的时候公司会回顾这一年的业绩。
example.pinyin: Niánzhōng de shíhou gōngsī huì huígù zhè yī nián de yèjì.
example.english: At year's end, the company reviews its performance for the year.
example.fact: At Carl Sagan's request, Voyager 1 turned its camera around in 1990 to take one last look back at Earth from about 3.7 billion miles away — the resulting 'Pale Blue Dot' photograph shows the planet as a single pixel of light against the vastness of space.

examples.hanzi: 回顾过去，我觉得自己成长了很多。
examples.pinyin: Huígù guòqù, wǒ juéde zìjǐ chéngzhǎng le hěn duō.
examples.english: Looking back, I feel I have grown a lot.

examples.hanzi: 这个展览回顾了城市的发展历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhǎnlǎn huígù le chéngshì de fāzhǎn lìshǐ.
examples.english: This exhibition looks back at the city's history of development.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 划 slice; 刷 is brushing or scraping, as in 刷牙 brush teeth.

example.hanzi: 我每天刷牙两次。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuā yá liǎng cì.
example.english: I brush my teeth twice a day.
example.fact: 刷 covers all kinds of brushing: 刷牙 (brush teeth), 刷墙 (paint a wall), and 刷卡 (swipe a card). A modern sense is scrolling or repeating, as in 刷手机 ('scroll on one's phone').

examples.hanzi: 吃完晚饭要刷碗。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán wǎnfàn yào shuā wǎn.
examples.english: You have to wash the dishes after dinner.

examples.hanzi: 你可以刷卡付款。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ shuākǎ fùkuǎn.
examples.english: You can pay by card.

components.note: 虍 (tiger head) — the striped head and body of a tiger; also in 虑 lǜ, 虚 xū.

example.hanzi: 动物园里有一只大老虎。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī dà lǎohǔ.
example.english: There is a big tiger in the zoo.
example.fact: 虎 usually appears as 老虎; it is a zodiac sign and a symbol of courage. 马虎 ('horse-tiger') is a funny word meaning careless, and 虎头蛇尾 describes starting strong and ending weakly.

examples.hanzi: 他属虎,今年二十四岁。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǔ hǔ, jīnnián èrshísì suì.
examples.english: He was born in the year of the tiger and is 24.

examples.hanzi: 你别马虎,再检查一遍。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié mǎhu, zài jiǎnchá yí biàn.
examples.english: Don't be careless; check it once more.

components.note: 子 (child) — marks children and offspring, as in 孩 child, 学 study, 字; 孙 is a grandchild, the child of a child.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 爷爷最喜欢带着孙子去公园。
example.pinyin: Yéye zuì xǐhuan dàizhe sūnzi qù gōngyuán.
example.english: Grandpa likes taking his grandson to the park most of all.
example.fact: The 'grandmother hypothesis' in evolutionary biology proposes that human females evolved unusually long post-reproductive lifespans specifically because grandmothers who helped raise grandchildren improved those children's survival odds — a pattern rarely seen in other mammals.

examples.hanzi: 他的孙子今年刚上小学。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sūnzi jīnnián gāng shàng xiǎoxué.
examples.english: His grandson has just started primary school this year.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶有两个孙子和一个孙女。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai yǒu liǎng gè sūnzi hé yí gè sūnnǚ.
examples.english: Grandma has two grandsons and one granddaughter.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 把 is to grasp.
巴 (bā) gives the sound: 把 bǎ is close, as in 爸 bà and 吧 ba.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 握 is to grasp, as in 握手 handshake.
屋 (wū) — near sound — 握 is wò; 屋 also sounds out 幄 wò.

example.hanzi: 我们要把握住这个难得的机会。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎwò zhù zhège nándé de jīhuì.
example.english: We must seize this rare opportunity.
example.fact: Peregrine falcons seize their prey mid-air by folding their wings and diving at speeds exceeding 240 mph, making them the fastest animals on Earth — the strike, called a 'stoop,' can generate enough force to kill a pigeon instantly.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试你有把握吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì nǐ yǒu bǎwò ma?
examples.english: Are you confident about this exam?

examples.hanzi: 我没有十足的把握能赢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu shízú de bǎwò néng yíng.
examples.english: I'm not completely sure I can win.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and feelings in old forms, as in 妒, 嫉; 嫌 is to dislike.
兼 (jiān) — near sound — 嫌 is xián; 兼 also sounds out 谦 qiān and 歉 qiàn.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名抢劫案的嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yī míng qiǎngjié àn de xiányírén.
example.english: Police arrested a suspect in the robbery case.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard tool for identifying criminal suspects after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it in 1892 to solve a murder case, matching a bloody thumbprint at the scene to the victim's mother — one of the first murder convictions based on fingerprint evidence.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在审问那名嫌疑人。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài shěnwèn nà míng xiányírén.
examples.english: The police are questioning the suspect.

examples.hanzi: 监控拍到了嫌疑人的脸。
examples.pinyin: Jiānkòng pāi dào le xiányírén de liǎn.
examples.english: The surveillance camera captured the suspect's face.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
灬 (fire) — the four-dot form of 火, as in 热 hot, 点 point, 煮 cook; 烈 is blazing, then intense.
列 (liè) gives the sound exactly: 烈 liè, also in 裂 liè (split).

example.hanzi: 两队之间的比赛非常激烈。
example.pinyin: Liǎng duì zhījiān de bǐsài fēicháng jīliè.
example.english: The match between the two teams was extremely intense.
example.fact: Male elephant seals fight fierce, sometimes bloody battles for beachmaster status during breeding season, rearing up to slam their chests together — the winner may father the vast majority of pups on a beach, while most other males father none at all.

examples.hanzi: 他们为这个问题展开了激烈的讨论。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wèi zhège wèntí zhǎnkāi le jīliè de tǎolùn.
examples.english: They had a heated discussion about this issue.

examples.hanzi: 现在找工作的竞争很激烈。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài zhǎo gōngzuò de jìngzhēng hěn jīliè.
examples.english: Competition for jobs is fierce these days.

components.note: 户 (door) — the door family: 房 room, 所 place. 扁 was the inscribed board hung over a door, hence 'sign, plaque', then 'flat' (扁平).
册 (bound strips, a book) — what is written on the board. 扁 is also the sound part of 编 biān, 偏 piān, 篇 piān, 遍 biàn, 骗 piàn.

example.hanzi: 轮胎被扎扁了。
example.pinyin: Lúntāi bèi zhā biǎn le.
example.english: The tire got punctured and went flat.
example.fact: 扁 means flat or squashed (扁平), and informally 'to beat someone up': 我要扁你! The same character is read piān in 扁舟 (a small boat) and biǎn can also describe a flat bean 扁豆.

examples.hanzi: 这个气球被压扁了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qìqiú bèi yā biǎn le.
examples.english: This balloon got squashed flat.

examples.hanzi: 他的鼻子有点扁。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bízi yǒudiǎn biǎn.
examples.english: His nose is a bit flat.

components.note: 去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 他不小心把钱包丢掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn bǎ qiánbāo diūdiào le.
example.english: He accidentally lost his wallet.
example.fact: Rubber ducks and sneakers from a 1990 cargo spill in the Pacific became unlikely tools for oceanographers studying ocean currents — tracking where the thousands of lost shoes washed ashore over the following years helped refine models of the North Pacific gyre's circulation.

examples.hanzi: 这些旧报纸可以丢掉了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē jiù bàozhǐ kěyǐ diūdiào le.
examples.english: These old newspapers can be thrown away.

examples.hanzi: 别丢掉这个好机会。
examples.pinyin: Bié diūdiào zhège hǎo jīhuì.
examples.english: Don't let this great chance slip away.

meanings: camera (abbr. for 照相機|照相机[zhao4 xiang4 ji1])

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 她用相机拍下了日落的美景。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng xiàngjī pāixià le rìluò de měijǐng.
example.english: She used her camera to capture the beautiful sunset.
example.fact: The first permanent photograph, taken around 1826 or 1827 by Nicéphore Niépce, required an exposure time of about eight hours pointed out a window — the hazy resulting image of rooftops and a barn is the oldest surviving camera photograph.

examples.hanzi: 旅行的时候我一定会带相机。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng de shíhou wǒ yídìng huì dài xiàngjī.
examples.english: I always bring a camera when I travel.

examples.hanzi: 这台相机的电池没电了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái xiàngjī de diànchí méi diàn le.
examples.english: This camera's battery has run out.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 授 is to hand over, to give.
受 (shòu) sounds exactly like 授.
木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.

example.hanzi: 公司授权他代表签署合同。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī shòuquán tā dàibiǎo qiānshǔ hétong.
example.english: The company authorized him to sign the contract on its behalf.
example.fact: Modern computer security borrows a distinction formalized in 1970s access-control research, which separated 'authentication' (proving who you are) from 'authorization' (determining what you're allowed to do) — a split still fundamental to how banks and governments secure digital systems today.

examples.hanzi: 没有授权，你不能使用这张照片。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu shòuquán, nǐ bù néng shǐyòng zhè zhāng zhàopiàn.
examples.english: Without authorization, you cannot use this photo.

examples.hanzi: 经理已经授权她处理这件事。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ yǐjīng shòuquán tā chǔlǐ zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: The manager has authorized her to handle this matter.

components.note: 氵 (water) — sweat is water of the body; also in 河 river, 汤 soup.
干 (gān) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 旱 hàn and 焊 hàn.

example.hanzi: 他跑得满头大汗。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de mǎntóu dà hàn.
example.english: He ran until sweat was pouring from his head.
example.fact: 汗 is sweat: 出汗, 流汗, 冷汗 (cold sweat). 汗 is read hán in 可汗 (khan, a Mongolian ruler), so the same character can be a title; 汗颜 means 'to blush with shame'.

examples.hanzi: 天气太热,我出了一身汗。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè, wǒ chū le yì shēn hàn.
examples.english: It's so hot that I'm drenched in sweat.

examples.hanzi: 运动以后要及时擦汗。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng yǐhòu yào jíshí cā hàn.
examples.english: Wipe off the sweat promptly after exercising.

components.note: 象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这朵云看起来象是一只兔子。
example.pinyin: Zhè duǒ yún kànqǐlái xiàng shì yī zhī tùzi.
example.english: This cloud looks as if it's a rabbit.
example.fact: The tendency to see meaningful shapes, like faces or animals, in random patterns such as clouds is called pareidolia — it's thought to be a byproduct of a brain wired to spot faces quickly, since rapidly recognizing a face offered our ancestors a survival advantage.

examples.hanzi: 他的表情象是在想什么心事。
examples.pinyin: Tā de biǎoqíng xiàngshì zài xiǎng shénme xīnshì.
examples.english: His expression looks as if he's thinking about something.

examples.hanzi: 屋里很安静，象是没有人在家。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ hěn ānjìng, xiàngshì méiyǒu rén zài jiā.
examples.english: It's quiet inside, as if no one is home.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.hanzi: 孩子们的笑声充满了欢乐。
example.pinyin: Háizimen de xiàoshēng chōngmǎn le huānlè.
example.english: The children's laughter was full of joy.
example.fact: A 2005 University of Maryland study found that laughter measurably relaxes blood vessels: watching a stressful film narrowed participants' blood vessels, while watching a comedy widened them, an effect on blood flow the researchers compared to light exercise.

examples.hanzi: 新年的晚会上充满了欢乐的气氛。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián de wǎnhuì shàng chōngmǎn le huānlè de qìfēn.
examples.english: The New Year party was full of joyful atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 祝你们一家人幸福欢乐。
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐmen yì jiā rén xìngfú huānlè.
examples.english: Wishing your family happiness and joy.

components.note: 龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.
贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 贩 is to trade goods.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 贩 fàn is close to 饭 fàn.

example.hanzi: 警方成功抓获了一名毒贩。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng chénggōng zhuōhuò le yī míng dúfàn.
example.english: Police successfully caught a drug dealer.
example.fact: Opium smuggling into China by British traders in the 19th century grew so large-scale that it triggered the First Opium War (1839–1842); the conflict ended with China ceding Hong Kong to Britain, one of history's starkest examples of a drug trade reshaping geopolitics.

examples.hanzi: 毒贩通常很狡猾，不容易被抓到。
examples.pinyin: Dúfàn tōngcháng hěn jiǎohuá, bù róngyì bèi zhuādào.
examples.english: Drug dealers are usually cunning and hard to catch.

examples.hanzi: 那名毒贩被判了十年。
examples.pinyin: Nà míng dúfàn bèi pàn le shí nián.
examples.english: That drug trafficker was sentenced to ten years.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the top part, as in 和 and 秋. Memory aid: a woman (女) bending under a bundle of grain; grain plus woman gives 'bend / entrust', now 'appoint'.
女 (woman) — the bottom part and radical, as in 她 she and 妈 mom. Here it hints at a yielding, bending figure rather than a woman.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 律师向委托人解释了案件的进展。
example.pinyin: Lǜshī xiàng wěituōrén jiěshì le ànjiàn de jìnzhǎn.
example.english: The lawyer explained the progress of the case to the client.
example.fact: The legal concept of a trust, where one party manages assets for a client's benefit, traces back to medieval English 'uses' devised by knights heading off on the Crusades, who transferred land to a trusted friend to manage while they were away — an arrangement that evolved into modern trust law.

examples.hanzi: 律师必须保护委托人的利益。
examples.pinyin: Lǜshī bìxū bǎohù wěituōrén de lìyì.
examples.english: A lawyer must protect the interests of the client.

examples.hanzi: 委托人今天来办公室签了合同。
examples.pinyin: Wěituōrén jīntiān lái bàngōngshì qiān le hétong.
examples.english: The client came to the office today to sign the contract.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 他的月收入比去年增加了不少。
example.pinyin: Tā de yuè shōurù bǐ qùnián zēngjiā le bù shǎo.
example.english: His monthly income has increased quite a bit compared to last year.
example.fact: The Gini coefficient, a number between 0 and 1 used to measure income inequality within a country, was developed by Italian statistician Corrado Gini in 1912 — a score of 0 represents perfect equality, while 1 represents a hypothetical situation where a single person holds all the income.

examples.hanzi: 他们家的收入主要靠开小店。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiā de shōurù zhǔyào kào kāi xiǎo diàn.
examples.english: Their family income mainly comes from running a small shop.

examples.hanzi: 这个词典收入了五万个词条。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cídiǎn shōurù le wǔ wàn gè cítiáo.
examples.english: This dictionary includes fifty thousand entries.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.

example.hanzi: 老弟，好久不见，最近怎么样？
example.pinyin: Lǎodì, hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?
example.english: Old pal, long time no see, how have you been lately?
example.fact: A famous 75-year Harvard study following the same group of men from young adulthood into old age found that close, warm relationships were the single strongest predictor of health and happiness in later life — stronger than wealth, fame, or even cholesterol levels.

examples.hanzi: 老弟，这顿饭我来请。
examples.pinyin: Lǎodì, zhè dùn fàn wǒ lái qǐng.
examples.english: Buddy, this meal is on me.

examples.hanzi: 老弟，你放心，这事包在我身上。
examples.pinyin: Lǎodì, nǐ fàngxīn, zhè shì bāo zài wǒ shēn shàng.
examples.english: Don't worry, pal, leave this to me.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 恕 is a forgiving heart.
如 (rú) is a loose hint for shù.

example.hanzi: 请恕我直言，这个计划有问题。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shù wǒ zhíyán, zhège jìhuà yǒu wèntí.
example.english: Forgive my bluntness, but this plan has problems.
example.fact: 恕 is the Confucian ideal of reciprocity and forgiveness: Confucius defined it as 'do not do to others what you would not want done to you'. It survives in 宽恕 (to forgive) and polite formulas like 恕我直言.

examples.hanzi: 恕我不能参加你的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Shù wǒ bù néng cānjiā nǐ de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: Please forgive me for not being able to attend your wedding.

examples.hanzi: 这样的错误不可饶恕。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng de cuòwù bù kě ráoshù.
examples.english: Such a mistake is unforgivable.

meanings: (Tw) to repeatedly nod one's head while dozing

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁, 钱, 银; 钓 is to fish with a metal hook.
勺 (sháo) is only a loose sound hint for diào.
鱼 (fish) — a picture of a fish: head on top, scaly body 田, tail 一. As a radical (鱼) it marks fish, as in 鲨, 鲜.

example.hanzi: 周末爸爸经常带我去河边钓鱼。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò bàba jīngcháng dài wǒ qù hébiān diàoyú.
example.english: On weekends, Dad often takes me fishing by the river.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found fish hooks made from shell dating back roughly 23,000 years at a cave site on Okinawa, among the oldest known fishing tools in the world — evidence that early humans there were already skilled anglers well before the last Ice Age ended.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷退休以后最爱钓鱼。
examples.pinyin: Yéye tuìxiū yǐhòu zuì ài diàoyú.
examples.english: Grandpa loves fishing most since he retired.

examples.hanzi: 我们在湖边钓鱼，钓了一下午。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài húbiān diàoyú, diào le yí xiàwǔ.
examples.english: We fished by the lake for a whole afternoon.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 从这里到市中心大约十公里。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào shì zhōngxīn dàyuē shí gōnglǐ.
example.english: It's about ten kilometers from here to downtown.
example.fact: The meter was originally defined in 1793 by French scientists as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator along a line through Paris — a definition later found to be slightly inaccurate, since the meter is now defined instead using the speed of light.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车一小时能开一百公里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē yì xiǎoshí néng kāi yì bǎi gōnglǐ.
examples.english: This car can go a hundred kilometers an hour.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上跑五公里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang pǎo wǔ gōnglǐ.
examples.english: I run five kilometers every morning.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks liquor, fermenting and tastes, as in 酒 liquor, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 酸 is sour, as vinegar and wine turn.
夋 (qūn) — loose sound hint (suān); same part in 俊 jùn.

example.hanzi: 这个橘子太酸了。
example.pinyin: Zhège júzi tài suān le.
example.english: This tangerine is too sour.
example.fact: 酸 is sour, and also an aching sensation in muscles (腰酸, 腿酸 'my legs ache') and a feeling of sadness (心酸, 'heartache'). One of the five tastes, 酸甜苦辣咸 begins with 酸.

examples.hanzi: 我运动后全身酸痛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yùndòng hòu quánshēn suāntòng.
examples.english: I ache all over after exercising.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢吃酸辣粉。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chī suānlàfěn.
examples.english: He likes eating hot and sour noodles.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 全班同学在操场上集合。
example.pinyin: Quán bān tóngxué zài cāochǎng shàng jíhé.
example.english: The whole class gathered on the sports field.
example.fact: Set theory, the mathematical study of collections of objects, was largely founded single-handedly by Georg Cantor in the 1870s — his radical claim that some infinities are larger than others provoked fierce resistance from contemporaries but now underlies nearly all of modern mathematics.

examples.hanzi: 明天早上八点在校门口集合。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn zài xiàoménkǒu jíhé.
examples.english: Meet at the school gate at eight tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 数学课上我们学了集合的概念。
examples.pinyin: Shùxué kè shàng wǒmen xué le jíhé de gàiniàn.
examples.english: In math class we learned the concept of sets.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
立 (stand) — the person-standing radical, as in 站 itself and 位 position; here it carries the meaning of standing.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound exactly: 站 zhàn, also in 战 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 我们在车站等了半个小时的火车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn děng le bàn gè xiǎoshí de huǒchē.
example.english: We waited half an hour for the train at the station.
example.fact: Grand Central Terminal in New York City has a ceiling mural of the night sky painted backwards; the more likely explanation, despite a popular legend blaming a copying error, is that it was meant to be viewed as if from beyond the stars, looking down at Earth.

examples.hanzi: 请问，最近的公交车站在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zuìjìn de gōngjiāo chēzhàn zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the nearest bus stop?

examples.hanzi: 我去车站接你，你几点到？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù chēzhàn jiē nǐ, nǐ jǐ diǎn dào?
examples.english: I'll pick you up at the station; what time do you arrive?
